text:
Jordan Lee: quick sync in-thread on gate types for Dedicated staged rollouts. For beta we said latency + 5xx + queue depth. Open question: what do we do when metrics are missing/late? pause-by-default vs “best effort”. Also need to decide how UI renders “missing metrics” vs “fail”.

Paula Mendes: +1. Product POV: operators need a deterministic answer. If we silently proceed on missing data we’ll get burned. But if we pause too aggressively, rollouts will be stuck all the time.

Logan Wright: from telemetry side: we *will* have occasional gaps (exporter restarts, partial region outage, scrapes lagging). esp for per-pool queue depth. So “pause on any missing sample” is going to be super noisy.

Sean Gallagher: SRE POV: I’d rather a noisy pause than a bad advance. For Dedicated we’re on the hook for latency SLOs. Missing metrics is basically “unknown risk”. We should fail safe.

Allison Grant: UI/ops POV: we need to distinguish three states clearly: PASS, FAIL, and NO_DATA. NO_DATA shouldn’t look like FAIL because action is different (check pipeline vs rollback).

Chloe Martin: +1 and we need a single status the stage state machine can consume. Today evaluator returns boolean pass/fail. We can extend to tristate and reason.

Jordan Lee: ok, so evaluator returns {pass|fail|no_data}? then stage logic: fail => hold (and maybe auto-rollback depending policy), no_data => hold (no auto-advance). That keeps policy deterministic.

Logan Wright: if we do NO_DATA -> hold, we need a definition. Like “insufficient samples in window” or “staleness > X”. Otherwise a single missed scrape holds.

Thomas Baird: proposing we define “metrics_freshness_slo”: require at least N points or M% coverage over evaluation window. Example: window=10m, step=30s => 20 expected points. Require >= 16 points (80%) and last point within 2m.

Paula Mendes: that matches the PRD language. Can we make defaults sane? For beta I’d like it not to be configurable per gate unless we have to.

Sean Gallagher: agreed on coverage threshold. Also we should surface “data latency” explicitly (how old is latest datapoint) so oncall can decide if it’s instrumentation vs real regression.

Mina Haddad: routing question: if stage is held due to NO_DATA, traffic split stays where it is. That’s fine. But we need to ensure we don’t oscillate weights due to evaluator flapping.

Jordan Lee: yes, state machine should be monotonic unless manual abort/rollback. i.e. no automatic revert on transient NO_DATA; just hold and notify.

Jada Williams: implementation detail: we already store GateEvaluationSummary in rollout status response. We can add fields: `data_coverage_pct`, `last_sample_age_sec`, `no_data_reason`, and display them.

Allison Grant: please also add “query” link / dashboard link. Operators will click through. Even a static link to the dedicated-rollouts gate health dashboard is enough.

Logan Wright: careful on query exposure in UI. Don’t dump full PromQL w/ labels that include tenant/pool if we’re worried about leakage. But for operators ok.

Benji Okafor: on the control plane side, Gate definition currently has `metric`, `threshold`, `window`, `comparison`. We can add `min_coverage_pct` + `max_data_age` as optional with defaults.

Paula Mendes: question: do we treat partial metric availability (e.g., latency is there but queue depth missing) as NO_DATA for that gate only, but still allow stage to pass if other gates pass?

Sean Gallagher: no, stage should require *all configured gates* to PASS. If any gate is NO_DATA, stage should hold. That’s the point of having multiple gates.

Logan Wright: yup. Otherwise the operator thinks queue depth was checked when it wasn’t.

Jordan Lee: ok. So semantics: stage PASS if all gates PASS. stage FAIL if any gate FAIL. stage NO_DATA if no FAILs but at least one gate NO_DATA.

Chloe Martin: UX: how do we show that? In stage list maybe badge: “Held (Data unavailable)” vs “Held (Gate failed)”. And gate rows show “No data” with reason.

Allison Grant: exactly. Also add a warning icon when evaluator itself is lagging. We’ll have a separate gate-evaluator health signal.

Thomas Baird: metric cardinality note: if we add coverage_pct/last_sample_age per gate *per pool* that’s fine. But don’t add per-route dims. Dedicated pools can be high volume.

Logan Wright: +1. For example, queue depth is emitted per pool already. Latency/5xx should be aggregated per pool (not per model version) for gating. Otherwise we’ll blow up.

Mina Haddad: wait, for latency we probably want “candidate slice” vs “control slice” (stage traffic). How do we get per-stage metrics without per-request tags?

Jordan Lee: routing has deterministic allocation; we can tag requests with `rollout_stage_id` at the edge (low-card). That’s per pool *per stage*, bounded small (<=5). That seems ok.

Logan Wright: if we do that, we need to be disciplined: label = stage_id (small), pool_id (bounded by tenants), tenant_id (existing). That’s okay. Don’t add model_id + route + stage_id all together.

Paula Mendes: ok for beta scope: gate types = p95 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth. Missing metrics behavior = hold + label as NO_DATA. UI shows “Data unavailable” explicitly + freshness.

Sean Gallagher: also make default `max_data_age` tight-ish (2m?) so we don’t advance on stale. But not so tight it triggers constantly during scrape hiccups.

Thomas Baird: I’d suggest defaults: window=10m, min_coverage=80%, max_data_age=180s. These are tunable later.

Chloe Martin: can we add copy in UI: “Data coverage 65% (threshold 80%). Latest sample 6m old (threshold 3m).” That makes it obvious.

Allison Grant: yes, and add action hint: “Check metrics pipeline / exporter health” with link to runbook.

Jordan Lee: action items:
- @Benji Okafor add min_coverage_pct + max_data_age to Gate schema (defaulted)
- @Jada Williams update status API to include coverage + last sample age + reason enum
- @Chloe Martin / @Allison Grant align on UI strings + badge taxonomy
- @Logan Wright sanity check which metrics we can compute coverage on reliably

Paula Mendes: :thumbsup: I’ll update PRD wording + make sure beta messaging says “rollouts will pause if metrics unavailable”.

Logan Wright: one more: for “missing metrics” we should treat it as *no auto rollback*. Rolling back on NO_DATA could create a loop when telemetry is down.

Sean Gallagher: strongly agree. FAIL can trigger rollback (if policy says). NO_DATA should hold and page.

Jordan Lee: perfect. locking that in unless someone screams.

Ravi Menon: (late) +1. routing doesn’t care why it’s held, just needs stable weights. So holding on NO_DATA is safe.

Allison Grant: adding :eyes: — please ensure we emit an audit event when auto-hold happens w/ reason=NO_DATA vs FAIL, so compliance folks can see why it stopped.

Jordan Lee: good call. will thread to audit logging workstream.
